common.question: Where did you first want to keep reading? Which detail created that interest?
common.why: Locates the moment the story earns attention.

common.question: Where did you skim or lose the thread? Name the passage and what you were waiting to learn.
common.why: Separates a loss of interest from missing context.

common.question: Which detail would you most want preserved in a revision, and what would be lost without it?
common.why: Identifies strengths a revision might accidentally remove.

excerpt.label: A chapter or excerpt
excerpt.question: At the end of this excerpt, what did you expect to happen next, and why?
excerpt.why: Tests the promise of the excerpt without asking for a whole-book judgment.

draft.label: A complete working draft
draft.question: Which question felt resolved by the ending, and which still felt unfinished?
draft.why: Checks the payoff against the promises the reader noticed.

revised.label: A revised complete draft
revised.question: Where did the draft repeat information you already understood? Point to both passages if possible.
revised.why: Finds leftover explanations after a structural revision.

multiple-pov.label: Multiple viewpoints
multiple-pov.question: When the viewpoint changed, how quickly did you know whose perspective you were in? Point to a change that helped or disrupted you.

romance-subplot.label: Romance subplot
romance-subplot.question: Which relationship moment affected how you understood the main story? Where did the two feel disconnected?
romance-subplot.why: Checks whether the subplot changes the experience of the main plot.

series.label: Series opener
series.question: Which question belongs to this book, and which would you be happy to carry into another?
series.why: Distinguishes an unfinished local story from a welcome series promise.

unreliable.label: Unreliable narrator
unreliable.question: When did you first doubt the narrator, and what made you doubt them?
unreliable.why: Locates the difference between deliberate distrust and accidental confusion.

general.label: General fiction
general.focus: What draws you in, where do you lose the thread, and which passages shape those reactions?

questions.question: Which character choice was hardest to understand, and what did you expect instead?
questions.why: Locates a gap in the reader's understanding of motivation.

fantasy.label: Fantasy
fantasy.focus: Track the limits and cost of magic. Where do new world details help you follow a choice, and where do they interrupt the story?

questions.question: Before magic changed an outcome, what did you understand about its limits and cost? Which earlier detail established that?
questions.why: Checks whether a solution relies on a rule introduced too late.

questions.question: Which unfamiliar term could you understand from context, and which stopped you following the action?
questions.why: Separates immersive vocabulary from missing orientation.

questions.question: Which detail of the world changed what a character could choose? Which felt detached from the scene?
questions.why: Tests whether worldbuilding affects the story rather than only decorating it.

romance.label: Romance
romance.focus: Follow attraction, trust, and boundaries. Which actions make changes in the relationship feel earned?

questions.question: When did attraction begin to feel like trust? What did one character actually do to earn that change?
questions.why: Distinguishes an asserted bond from one built through actions.

questions.question: What seemed to keep the couple apart, and when did that obstacle become convincing or stop convincing you?
questions.why: Checks whether the relationship conflict holds beyond a convenient misunderstanding.

questions.question: Where did each person make a meaningful choice about the relationship? Where did one person's wishes become unclear?
questions.why: Examines agency and boundaries from the reader's perspective.

mystery.label: Mystery
mystery.focus: Track suspicions and the clues behind them. Which explanations fit the evidence available to you at each point?

questions.question: Who did you suspect before the reveal, and which specific clues led you there?
questions.why: Reconstructs the reader's theory from the evidence on the page.

questions.question: After the reveal, which earlier clue changed meaning? Which part of the explanation needed information you had not received?
questions.why: Checks the fairness of the solution.

questions.question: Which investigative step followed naturally from the evidence, and which felt like a lucky leap?
questions.why: Tests the chain between observation, deduction, and action.

questions.question: Which unanswered question were you most interested in solving at this point?
questions.why: Checks whether the investigation has given the reader a concrete mystery.

thriller.label: Thriller
thriller.focus: Track the threat, deadline, and choices under pressure. Where do the stakes feel immediate, and where does urgency fade?

questions.question: What did you think would happen if the protagonist failed, and when did that consequence become clear?
questions.why: Checks the reader's understanding of the stakes.

questions.question: When did you feel time running out? Which action or detail made the deadline tangible?
questions.why: Separates a stated deadline from experienced urgency.

questions.question: Which escape or reversal was hardest to believe, and what established rule or detail shaped your doubt?
questions.why: Locates credibility problems without requiring every twist to be predictable.
